transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... it's just getting really hard at work. I'm a jeweler, you know, mostly custom work and repairs. And lately, when someone asks me a simple question, like... oh, just asking when a ring sizing will be ready. I try to answer, but my brain just... my answer starts going from the invoices we just got from the supplier, and then I'm talking about the garden soil I need to pick up for my tomatoes, and then somehow I'm on about the mortgage papers I need to sign. And I can just see them losing me. Their eyes kind of glaze over. It's like that time my neighbor asked if I'd seen her cat, and I ended up telling her all about the history of the neighborhood watch program, which honestly, hasn't been the same since Brenda moved away. Brenda made the best potato salad. But anyway, yeah, I just can't seem to give a straight answer to a simple question anymore without wandering off into the weeds.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are so jumbled or disconnected that even you have trouble following them, like one idea doesn't logically lead to the next?

Yeah, that's exactly what I meant a second ago about the ring repairs. It's... it's exactly like that. I'll be trying to explain something simple, and then my brain just skips from the invoices over to the garden soil or the mortgage papers, and even I'm sitting there wondering how I got there. The ideas just don't link up the way they're supposed to. 

It's exhausting because I used to be so meticulous, you know? You really have to be, with jewelry. I used to have these little velvet trays for everything on my workbench. Sapphires in one, emeralds in another. Emeralds are actually really fragile to work with, they have these little natural flaws inside them that look like branches or leaves... jewelers call it the *jardin*, which is French for garden. Which I guess is funny since I was just talking about my tomato garden. The aphids are just terrible this year, I've tried neem oil and everything. 

But um... what were we just saying? Oh, right, following my own thoughts. Yes. It feels very jumbled, like I just can't keep a straight line in my head anymore.
Do you find yourself speaking so fast that others have trouble keeping up or interrupt to ask you to slow down?

No, I don't think I talk too fast. It's more just... wandering, like I said. People don't tell me to slow down, they just look confused. Although, my sister did tell me to slow down once, but that was when we were driving to Cape Cod. She gets terrible carsickness. We used to go every summer when we were kids, and my mother would make us these little sandwiches with the crusts cut off. I still cut the crusts off my sandwiches sometimes. It just tastes better, you know? The crust gets so dry, especially if you buy that whole wheat bread from the bakery down the street. They bake it fresh every morning, and the smell is just wonderful when I walk past on my way to the shop. But no, nobody really says I speak too fast. Just that they can't follow me.
Have you ever felt like you couldn't stop talking, or that you had so much to say that you couldn't get it all out fast enough?

No, I don't really feel like I have too much to say, or that I can't stop. It's not a pressure or anything like that. It's just that once I start, the path sort of... winds around. Like I'm walking through the woods instead of taking the highway. Speaking of the woods, my husband and I used to go hiking up in the White Mountains before he passed. He had this old walking stick he carved himself out of a piece of hickory. Hickory is such a hard wood, really difficult to carve, but he was so patient. He used to sit on the porch for hours just whittling away. I still have that stick in the umbrella stand by the front door. The umbrella stand is actually an old brass artillery shell from the First World War, my grandfather brought it back. It needs a good polishing, actually. Brass gets so tarnished if you don't keep up with it, especially with the humidity we've been having. But... no, I don't feel like I'm talking too much or too fast. It's just hard to stay on the main road.
Do you find that your attention is easily pulled away by things going on around you, like sounds or sights, more than usual?

Not really, no. I don't think I get distracted by noises or things happening around me. I mean, I hear them, like... I can hear that clock ticking on your wall right now. It's a nice clock, actually. Looks like mahogany. I don't work on clocks myself, the gears are completely different from setting stones, though my friend Arthur, he runs a clock repair shop just two towns over. He fixed this beautiful antique carriage clock for me last winter. I found it at an estate sale. I just love estate sales, you can find the most incredible things sitting in cardboard boxes because people just don't know what they have. Last time I went, I found a set of sterling silver spoons. They were tarnished completely black, of course, but I knew exactly how to clean them up. I use this special polishing paste at my workbench... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, being pulled away by sounds. No, I don't think my attention gets pulled away by things like that any more than it ever did.
Have you noticed any change in how much sleep you need lately? Like feeling rested after only a few hours of sleep or not needing as much sleep as you used to?

No, I don't think my sleep has changed like that. I've been sleeping my usual amount, I suppose. I definitely don't feel rested if I only get a few hours. I need my full night's sleep, especially with the work I do. My hands have to be so steady when I'm setting stones, you know? Even the slightest tremor and you can chip a diamond, or worse, an emerald. Emeralds are so brittle, they have all those little inclusions they call the 'jardin'—it means garden in French, because it looks like little branches or moss inside the stone. It's beautiful, really, but it makes them so fragile. I had a client once bring in her grandmother's emerald ring to be resized, and I was terrified the whole time I was working on it. The setting was this intricate filigree from the 1920s, platinum, which is incredibly difficult to work with because it requires such a high heat to solder. You need a special torch for it, not just the standard jeweler's torch. I actually had to upgrade my ventilation system in the shop when I started working with platinum more often. The fumes can be quite bad for you if you're not careful. But... no, I haven't noticed needing less sleep. I still need my regular hours.
Have you noticed that you're not enjoying the things you used to enjoy as much lately, like your jewelry work or your garden?

Yes, actually. That's... well, it's been hard. I used to just love hunting around for old clasps at those estate sales I mentioned, and I was even planning to run these little jewelry-making classes in my shop. But lately, I just go in there and stare at the trays of stones and findings. It just feels like none of it is worth starting anymore. Which is strange, because I've always loved organizing my trays. I use these little velvet-lined compartments, the dark blue ones, because they make the silver really pop when you're looking at it. The blue velvet reminds me of this dress my mother used to wear when I was a little girl. She'd wear it to the Christmas Eve service at our church, the one with the big stained-glass windows. Those windows were magnificent, all that leaded glass. Working with lead came is a whole different skill set, very different from fine jewelry. You have to be so careful with the soldering irons they use, they're massive compared to my little torch. My uncle actually did stained glass as a hobby, he made this beautiful suncatcher for my kitchen window... but, yes, I just don't have the heart for my work right now. I just stare at it all.
Have you ever felt like you didn’t need as much sleep as usual, like you could function just fine on only a few hours of sleep?

No, I really haven't. Like I said earlier, I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get my full eight hours, I'm just a wreck the next day. I can't imagine functioning on just a few hours. My sister, though, she was one of those people who claimed she only needed four hours of sleep a night. She was a nurse, worked the night shift at County General for almost twenty years. I don't know how she did it, honestly. The fluorescent lights in those hospitals are just awful. They have this terrible greenish hum to them, you know? It completely washes out your complexion. Whenever I'd go visit her, I'd notice how everyone just looked so sickly under those lights. It's the exact opposite of what you want in a jewelry shop. I use special daylight bulbs in my display cases so you can see the true color of the stones. Especially with sapphires, because if the lighting is too warm, a good blue sapphire can look almost black, and you lose all that beautiful saturation. I get my bulbs from this specialty lighting supplier out in Oregon... but anyway, no, I've never felt like I didn't need my sleep. I definitely need it.
Have you noticed yourself being more critical of your work or feeling like you're not good at things that you used to be confident in?

Yes, it's... it's all the time now. I just look at everything I do and think about how I'm ruining things. Like, we took on this mortgage for the shop, and I keep thinking I've completely ruined our future by doing that. I'm just a burden. I replay every single late repair in my head, every awkward conversation with a customer, and it just proves I'm not good at this anymore. Mortgages are so complicated now, aren't they? The paperwork we had to sign was just mountains of it. The notary we used, Mr. Henderson, he had this incredible fountain pen. It was a vintage Montblanc, the Meisterstück, I think. You don't see people using real fountain pens much anymore. The nib was 14-karat gold, which is actually the perfect alloy for a nib because it has enough flex to give you variation in your line weight, but it won't corrode from the ink. I've repaired a few gold nibs in my time, mostly straightening them out when someone dropped them point-down. It's delicate work, you have to use these tiny little burnishing tools... but yes, I just feel like I'm a burden and I've messed everything up with the shop and the house.

There is no evidence of manic or hypomanic symptoms, which rules out bipolar disorders. The patient also does not endorse pressured speech, decreased need for sleep, or distractibility, which makes schizophrenia and related thought disorders less likely. This turn ruled out manic/hypomanic features, narrowing the differential from previous candidates (F21, F34.9).
